name: Special Joint City Council/Housing Authority
minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  SPECIAL JOINT CITY COUNCIL/HOUSING AUTHORITY
  MEETING MINUTES
  TUESDAY, MAY 12, 2026

CALL TO ORDER  The Special Joint meeting of the City Council South Gate Housing
  Authority was called to order by Joshua Barron, Mayor/Chairperson at
  5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL  City Clerk Yodit Glaze, City Clerk/Recording Secretary

PRESENT  Mayor/Chairperson Joshua Barron, Vice Mayor/Vice Chairperson Al Rios,
  Council/Authority Member Maria Davila, Council/Authority Member Gil
  Hurtado; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager/Executive Director
  Rob Houston, City Attorney/Authority Counsel Raúl F. Salinas

LATE  Council/Authority Member Maria del Pilar Avalos
1
DEVELOPMENT  It is recommended that the City Council and Housing Authority:

  a. Approve the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) among the City
  of South Gate (Contract No. 2026-33-CC), the South Gate Housing
  Authority (Contract No. 2026-01-HA), and Habitat for Humanity of
  Greater Los Angeles or Partnership Housing, Inc. (Developer) to
  establish initial terms for negotiating a Disposition, Development and
  Loan Agreement (DDA) and an Affordable Housing and Loan
  Agreement (AHA); and

  b. Authorize the Chairperson of the South Gate Housing Authority and
  Mayor or authorized designee to execute the MOU in a form approved
  by the City Attorney.

  Carol Averell, Housing Manager, gave the presentation.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked whether staff will be presenting
  a detailed financial analysis before any binding agreements with Habitat
  are considered or executed.

  Ms. Averell replied in the affirmative and stated that the city is already in
  the process of developing the Disposition and Development Agreement.
  She explained that the agreement will be presented to the Council and
  Housing Authority at a later date, along with an item regarding the
  allocation of any City funding for this project. She noted that such an
  allocation is required in order for Habitat to work with the city and
  provide a pro forma and analysis of the financing and all funding sources
  that will be included in the project.

  MINUTES OF MAY 12, 2026

  Council/Authority Member Avalos stated that under Security and
  Covenants, it indicates that if a buyer decides to sell before the 45-year
  period is over, they must first offer the property directly to the developer.

  Ms. Averell explained that this requirement is part of Habitat for
  Humanity’s program. Habitat holds the first right of rescission, meaning
  that if a homeowner chooses to sell, the developer has the right to take
  back the property and then select another qualified low-income family to
  purchase it.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked whether the developer would
  purchase the property at market value or at the original price at which it
  was initially sold.

  Patrick Sunpanich, Senior Director for Government Affairs with Habitat
  for Humanity, responded that the property would be purchased at the
  market rate at that time.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked about the South Gate loan.

  Ms. Averell responded by outlining the various funding sources the city
  has applied for in connection with this project. She explained that the City
  has allocated HOME funds specifically for this development. In addition,
  the City has secured state funding, designated PHA funds for the project,
  and has applied for CalHome funding to support mortgage assistance.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos inquired about the DTSC grant funding
  that Habitat has received and the total amount awarded.

  Naomi Zahler, Associate Director of Public Funding and Contracts for
  Habitat, stated that she believes the DTSC grant amount is $800,000.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos further asked whether there were any
  estimates indicating that remediation costs might exceed the DTSC grant
  amount.

  Ms. Averell believes that pretty much most of the money is going to be
  utilized for that remediation. The remediation is quite costly. She also
  stated the city allocated CDBG funds for the demolition of the structure.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked what preliminary risks or
  uncertainties staff would like the Council/Housing Authority to be aware
  of at this stage, if any.

  Mr. Perez stated that it will be important for the city to resume remediation
  work, including demolition of the building. He emphasized that no
  approvals for the project are being considered at this meeting. The project
  will still require future approval by both the Planning Commission and the
  City Council.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked whether there was anything in
  the proposed MOU that staff recommended the Council or Housing
  Authority modify prior to approval, or if staff was satisfied with the
  document as presented.

  Mr. Perez stated that staff are satisfied with the MOU as written and
  recommends moving it forward to the Planning Commission and the City
  Council for future consideration.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked if there were any external
  deadlines, such as funding cycles, that could affect the project’s
  completion timeline.

  Ms. Averell stated that for CDBG funding, the project must be completed
  by the end of the year. She also noted that DTSC’s deadline is tied to the
  completion of the remediation work.

  Vice Mayor/Vice Chairperson Rios asked how much the City and Habitat
  for Humanity have spent to date and what the projected total cost of the
  project will be.

  City Manager/Executive Director Houston clarified for anyone who may
  be new to the City’s housing-related funding discussions over the past
  year that none of the funding for this project comes from the General
  Fund.

  Ms. Averell explained that projects of this type rely on multiple funding
  sources.

  Ms. Zahler stated the spending of about $200,000 of the DTSC fund so far.
  That’s just for remediation and doesn’t have the exact total for the
  remediation. DTSC has not expressed concern for the funding, especially
  since DTSC have waived the fees on their end. She also mentioned that
  Habitat for LA is exploring a lot of funds for the development, including
  new market tax credits and LACAHSA funds.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked how much additional funding the
  City anticipates contributing to this specific project, excluding General
  Fund dollars.

  Page 3 of 5
 SPECIAL JOINT CITY COUNCIL AND HOUSING AUTHORITY MEETING
  MINUTES OF MAY 12, 2026

  Ms. Averell responded that the HOME funds represent the final City-
  controlled funding source currently committed. She explained that the city
  must still evaluate all other funding sources that Habitat for Humanity will
  bring to the project. This evaluation will be part of the financial analysis
  conducted through the pro forma to determine the City’s total contribution.
  As an example, she noted that the city applied for $5 million in CalHome
  funding to support mortgage assistance for two affordable housing
  projects, and the full amount was awarded. Habitat will utilize at least half
  of those funds to provide up to $200,000 in mortgage assistance for the
  fourteen (14) units.

  Council/Authority Member Hurtado and Mayor/Chairperson Barron
  expressed that they are looking forward to seeing this project get off the
  ground.

  City Attorney/Authority Counsel Salinas reiterated that he previously
  served on the Board of Directors for Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los
  Angeles, a role he was proud to hold. He clarified that he no longer serves
  on the fiduciary board and currently participates only as a member of the
  Ameritas Board. He further stated that he has no legal obligations to the
  organization and does not receive any income from it.

  Council/Authority Member Hurtado stated that when the property is
  eventually sold, there will be a profit because the original appraisal value
  is no longer accurate. He added that the proceeds would return to the
  housing program.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked whether, once all the properties
  are sold, the City will release the titles to the new homeowners indicating
  that the City-provided mortgage has been fully paid off.

  Ms. Averell clarified that under the mortgage assistance program,
  homeowners will still be responsible for making certain mortgage
  payments. She explained that in some cases the City may structure the
  assistance as deferred, meaning repayment would occur upon sale,
  transfer, or refinancing of the property. She added that the city is currently
  finalizing the program guidelines.

  Council/Authority Member Avalos asked whether the City would recover
  any of the funds it contributes.

  Ms. Averell responded that the city would receive a portion back.

  Mr. Sunpanich added that repayment structures vary depending on the
  municipality partnering with Habitat for Humanity.

EMAILS  Mario  Dominguez,  a South  Gate resident,  raised  concerns  regarding  soil
  contamination  at the proposed  14 town  home  development  and requested
  information  on the timeline  for remediation  and disposal  of the
  contaminated  soil. He also asked about next steps following  remediation
  including  site development  plans,  additional  testing  and urges the city to
  avoid  delays  experienced  in the past projects.

  Council/Authority  Member  Hurtado  motioned,  seconded  by
  Mayor/Chairperson  Barron  to approve  items A & B.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council/Authority,  Avalos,  yes; Council/Authority
  Hurtado,  yes; Council/Authority  Davila,  yes; Vice Mayor/Vice
  Chairperson  Rios, yes; Mayor/Chairperson  Barron,  yes.

ADJOURNMENT  Mayor/Chairperson  Barron  unanimously  adjourned  the meeting  at 5:28
  p.m. and seconded  by Council/Authority  Member  Hurtado.

PASSED  and APPROVED  this 26"  day of May  2026.
